classification.difficultyReason: Interpret differently oriented prisms, find missing triangle dimensions using Pythagoras, and assemble all face areas. The equilateral end requires constructing an altitude and halving its base without a drawn guide.

content.prompt: Use Pythagoras’ Theorem $h^2=a^2+b^2$ to find unknown lengths and hence calculate the surface area of these solids. Round to 1 d.p. where necessary.

spec.description: Upright triangular prism with right-angle marks on both triangular ends and one dashed rear lower edge. Ordinary source blue and red strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Right triangular cross-section with perpendicular sides 3 m and 4 m; prism length 7 m. The hypotenuse is not supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: All dimensions and angle marks are permanent givens; the missing length and surface area are withheld.

answer.worked:
Let $c$ be the missing side of the triangular end.
$$\begin{align*}c^2&=3^2+4^2\\c&=5\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
Two triangles: $2\times\frac{3\times4}{2}=12\text{ m}^2$.
Rectangles: $3\times7=21\text{ m}^2$, $4\times7=28\text{ m}^2$ and $5\times7=35\text{ m}^2$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total surface area}&=12+21+28+35\\\text{Total surface area}&=96\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Oblique triangular prism with right-angle marks on corresponding triangular ends. The rear triangular hypotenuse is dashed, as shown in the PDF. Ordinary coloured strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Right triangular ends have one leg 7 cm and hypotenuse 10 cm; the longitudinal edge is 8 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and right-angle marks appear.

answer.worked:
Let $c$ be the missing side of the triangular end.
$$\begin{align*}c^2&=10^2-7^2\\c&=\sqrt{51}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Two triangles: $2\times\frac{7\sqrt{51}}{2}=7\sqrt{51}\text{ cm}^2$.
Rectangles: $7\times8=56\text{ cm}^2$, $10\times8=80\text{ cm}^2$ and $8\sqrt{51}\text{ cm}^2$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total surface area}&=7\sqrt{51}+56+80+8\sqrt{51}\\\text{Total surface area}&=136+15\sqrt{51}\\\text{Total surface area}&\approx243.1\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Isosceles triangular prism with double ticks on both front sloping sides, a dashed altitude and its right-angle mark. The altitude retains semantic red; the hidden rear edge is black and dashed.
spec.mathematics: Triangular base 8 cm, equal sides 5 cm and prism length 10 cm. The altitude meets the midpoint of the base.
spec.answerVisibility: The altitude is drawn but neither its length nor the half-base length is supplied.

answer.worked:
The altitude bisects the isosceles triangle’s base, giving $8\div2=4\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}h^2&=5^2-4^2\\h&=3\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Two triangles: $2\times\frac{8\times3}{2}=24\text{ cm}^2$.
Side rectangles: $2\times(10\times5)=100\text{ cm}^2$.
Bottom rectangle: $8\times10=80\text{ cm}^2$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total surface area}&=24+100+80\\\text{Total surface area}&=204\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upright prism with matching double ticks on all three upper triangular edges and a dashed lower rear edge. No altitude is added to the question figure.
spec.mathematics: Equilateral triangular cross-section with side 4 m and prism length 7 m.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source measurements and equal-side marks appear.

answer.worked:
The equilateral triangle’s altitude bisects its base, giving $4\div2=2\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}h^2&=4^2-2^2\\h&=\sqrt{12}=2\sqrt3\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
Two triangles: $2\times\frac{4\times2\sqrt3}{2}=8\sqrt3\text{ m}^2$.
Three rectangles: $3\times(4\times7)=84\text{ m}^2$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total surface area}&=8\sqrt3+84\\\text{Total surface area}&\approx97.9\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$
